template.name: target-design
template.source: Agreed baseline of a target design package that is still in progress. Expect structural updates when that phase closes; see references/changelog.md.

cover.lede: The {package}: {client}'s target architecture, how it is governed, onboarded, observed and operated, and the blueprint for building it in {next_phase}.

sections.title: Work plan
sections.intro: Four active-delivery weeks from kickoff to the design gate, followed by handoff and {client}'s response.

tasks.title: Draft and align platform responsibility boundaries
Draft target architecture and key ADRs
Map existing controls to platform enforcement points
Draft and align minimum control standards
Draft tracing, audit and cost requirements
Define evaluation approach and readiness checks
Draft the onboarding lifecycle and review gates
Create the manifest template and golden path
Define decision rights and governance cadence
Define support, incident, change and escalation model
Validate the design with workflow walkthroughs
Bring the deliverables together into the final architecture
Align the final architecture direction and finalize ADRs
Build the {next_phase} implementation plan from the findings

blocks.guide: One row per key session or review. Mark only the true decision points.
rows: Objectives, team, plan and ways of working
Review the baseline and align on the target architecture direction
Align on the final architecture before the design gate
Walk {client} through the design, templates, ADRs and backlog

blocks.guide: The recurring sessions and status reporting.
rows: Progress, decisions needed, risks and the week ahead
Working sessions on the target architecture and open questions
Progress, priorities, open questions and inputs needed from {client}

deliverable.title: Governance and Control Kit
deliverable.question: What standards and controls should govern the platform, and who is responsible for each?
sections: The control topics the kit covers.
{client}'s existing controls mapped to where the platform enforces them.
The minimum standard for each control topic.
The templates teams use to apply the standards.
Who is responsible for each control.
How exceptions are requested, approved and escalated.
How the kit integrates with {client}'s existing security services and tooling.
What a later implementation must provide.
A clear statement of which controls are designed only, and which are already deployed or certified.
criteria: Minimum standards for the listed control topics
Designed controls clearly distinguished from deployed or certified controls

deliverable.title: Onboarding Model
deliverable.question: How are capabilities such as agents, tools, services and workflows onboarded and managed through their lifecycle?
sections: The types of capability the model covers and how each is treated.
How a capability is registered and moves through its lifecycle.
The gates a capability passes, and who reviews it at each.

sections.title: Manifest template
sections.guide: Add one row per field every capability publishes.

sections: The recommended route to onboard a capability, step by step.
What an owner must provide before and after onboarding.
Representative capabilities taken through the model, and what the walkthroughs found.
What the onboarding model depends on.
criteria: Ownership and readiness or handoff requirements
Representative worked examples or walkthrough findings

deliverable.title: Observability and Evaluation Model
deliverable.question: What must be traced, logged, audited, costed and evaluated, and how is readiness demonstrated?
sections: What must be traced, and how traces are correlated across boundaries.
What must be logged and audited, and for how long.
The views operators and owners need.
How usage and cost are attributed and reported.
How agents, tools and models are evaluated.
The checks and evidence that show a capability is ready.
Who owns each part and what it depends on.
A clear statement of what is a requirement or design validation, and what is deployed monitoring, production testing or certification.
criteria: Requirements and design validation distinguished from deployed monitoring, production testing and certification

deliverable.title: Operating Model
deliverable.question: Who owns, decides, supports and escalates what across the platform?

sections.title: Ownership and RACI
sections.guide: Add one row per area: who is responsible, accountable, consulted and informed.

sections: The governance forums and how often they meet.
How the platform is supported, how incidents are handled, how change is controlled and how work is handed over.
How exceptions and escalations are handled.

sections.title: Unresolved ownership decisions
sections.guide: Add one row per unresolved ownership decision.

criteria: Support, incident, change and handoff responsibilities
Unresolved ownership decisions assigned an owner and next step

deliverable.title: Target Architecture
deliverable.question: What is {client}'s integrated target architecture, and which responsibilities, boundaries and decisions does it rest on?

sections.title: The target architecture
sections.guide: The final target architecture diagram, with a short caption. This is the single authoritative diagram and the first time the architecture is shown in the package; every detailed view below must be consistent with it.

sections: The principles the target architecture follows, as agreed with {client}.
The platforms the architecture covers and how each one participates.
What each platform and shared component is responsible for.

sections.title: Logical and physical patterns
sections.guide: The detailed views behind the target architecture diagram: logical patterns, physical deployment and trust boundaries. Each must be consistent with the target architecture diagram above.

sections: What the control plane does and how platforms integrate with it.
Where identity, trust and security boundaries sit, and how they are enforced.
How data, context, memory and state are handled across the platform.

The role of {client}'s existing platforms, and the capability matrix: what the platform needs, what {client} has, what existing products provide today and on their roadmap, gaps, overlaps and what to reuse.
What the representative workflow walkthroughs and demonstrations showed.

sections.title: Architecture decision records
sections.guide: Add one row per ADR, with the decision and rationale in full.

What changed between the baseline review and the final architecture, and why.
Assumptions, dependencies, limitations and open decisions
What remains open at handover, each with an owner and next step.

Identity, trust, data, context, state and security boundaries
Assumptions, dependencies, limitations and open decisions
Role of existing platforms and capability matrix
